hook: Here is a phone-free work block design that actually holds under pressure.
topic: Designing and protecting a phone-free work block
body:
**Here is a phone-free work block design that actually holds under pressure.**

Most people attempt phone-free work by putting the phone face-down on the desk. That is not a phone-free block. The phone is still in the room. The pull still exists. The mental bandwidth required to not reach for it is still being spent.

A real phone-free block has three components. Location, duration, and agreement.

Location: phone in a different physical space. Not on the desk, not in a drawer. A different room. Distance removes the reflex entirely rather than just blocking execution of it.

Duration: start at 45 minutes, not 90. The first time you run a phone-free block, 90 minutes feels architectural. 45 minutes is achievable today. Once 45 is automatic, move to 60, then 90. Stack the wins before you stack the time.

Agreement: if you have colleagues or a team, the block requires a single communication sent in advance. "I am unavailable from 9 to 10. Contact for emergencies is email." Most professional environments will accept this. The ones that will not are telling you something important about the environment, not about the protocol.

Run this block during your peak cognitive hours — typically the first 90 minutes after you start work. That is where the compound return lives.

One block. Every day. Non-negotiable.

Full scheduling system in the link in bio.
